routes.name: Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA)
routes.summary: A quick online permission for short UK visits if you don't need a visa. Needed for tourism, family visits, some business and for connecting through UK border control. It is not a guarantee of entry.

other: Applies to non-visa nationals (most of Europe, the Americas, Australia and many others). People who need a visa for visits use the Standard Visitor visa instead.
British and Irish citizens and people with UK permission to live, work or study don't need one.
Every traveler needs one, including babies and children.
One gov.uk news page listed a 16 GBP fee and the main ETA page lists 20 GBP. The main page figure is used. Confirm before showing users.

stay.note: Up to 6 months per visit. Valid for two years or until your passport expires, whichever is first, with multiple trips allowed (per a gov.uk news page).

steps: Apply on the official GOV.UK ETA service (gov.uk/eta/apply).
Get the approval before you travel.
Check expiry any time at gov.uk/check-eta.

sources.label: GOV.UK news: UK enforces digital permission to travel

routes.name: Visa-free visit (non-visa nationals, with ETA)
routes.summary: Citizens of countries not on the UK visa national list can visit without a visa, but now need an ETA first. Stays are usually up to 6 months.

other: Applies to every nationality not on the visa national list (115 countries and territories need a visa).
Hong Kong and Macao SAR passport holders, and Taiwan passport holders with an ID number in the passport, don't need a visa either.

routes.name: Standard Visitor visa
routes.summary: For visa nationals visiting the UK for tourism, seeing family, certain business activities, short study or medical treatment. Usually up to 6 months. You can't work or live here through repeat visits.

other: Needed if your nationality is on the 115-country visa national list.
Allowed: tourism, family visits, meetings and interviews, short courses up to 30 days, some paid engagements, volunteering up to 30 days, medical treatment.
Not allowed: working for a UK company, self-employment, public funds, marriage or civil partnership.

stay.note: Longer-term Standard Visitor visas exist for frequent visitors. The validity periods weren't on the page read.

routes.name: Transit visas (Visitor in Transit and Direct Airside Transit)
routes.summary: If you pass through UK border control and leave within 48 hours you may need a Visitor in Transit visa. If you stay airside without passing border control you may need a Direct Airside Transit visa. ETA holders don't need either.

other: You don't need a transit visa if you hold an ETA, a Standard Visitor visa, a Marriage Visitor visa, an EU Settlement Scheme family permit or a Home Office travel document.
Staying more than 48 hours or transiting often over 6 months needs a Standard Visitor visa instead.
Which transit visa applies depends on your nationality and whether you clear border control. Use the GOV.UK visa checker. The airside transit nationality list wasn't on the pages read.
Direct Airside Transit fee not confirmed.

stay.note: Visitor in Transit: leave within 48 hours.

routes.name: Skilled Worker visa
routes.summary: For people with a job offer from a Home Office approved UK employer in an eligible occupation. Lasts up to 5 years and can be extended. Settlement rules are changing, so check the latest ILR page.

income.note: Or the going rate for the job if higher. A reduced 33,400 GBP threshold applies in some cases. Different rules apply for healthcare, education and some extensions.

savings.note: Held 28 days. Skipped if you've held a UK visa for 12 months or your employer covers month one.

eligibility.language: Prove English (level not confirmed on pages read)
other: Certificate of sponsorship from a licensed employer.
Higher skilled jobs are eligible. Medium skilled jobs only if on the immigration salary list or temporary shortage list.
Partner and children can apply as dependants.
Settlement timing may change under earned settlement reforms. English level wasn't confirmed.

stay.note: Up to 5 years at a time, extendable.

fees.label: Salary list jobs, up to 3 years

routes.processing: Usually about 3 weeks from outside the UK, about 8 weeks from inside.

routes.name: Health and Care Worker visa
routes.summary: For qualified doctors, nurses, health professionals and adult social care professionals with a job offer from an approved UK employer. No healthcare surcharge. A separate government announcement said overseas recruitment of care workers is ending.

other: Certificate of sponsorship and minimum salary for the job (figures not on the page read).
You usually need to prove English.
A gov.uk announcement (May 2025) says new overseas recruitment of care workers stops. Exact closure date and current scope weren't confirmed, so check the page before applying.

sources.label: GOV.UK: Health and Care Worker visa
GOV.UK: Overseas recruitment for care workers to end

routes.name: Global Talent visa
routes.summary: For leaders or potential leaders in academia or research, arts and culture, or digital technology. Needs an endorsement unless you won an eligible prize. No job offer needed.

other: Endorsement required unless you hold an eligible prestigious prize.
Fields: academia or research, arts and culture, digital technology.
ILR after 3 or 5 years depending on field. 3 years used here. Settlement reforms may change timing.

stay.note: Up to 5 years at a time, extensions of 1 to 5 years.

routes.processing: Usually about 3 weeks from outside the UK, about 8 weeks from inside.

routes.name: High Potential Individual visa
routes.summary: For recent graduates of eligible top universities. Lasts 2 years, or 3 with a PhD. You can't extend it or settle on it, but you can switch to another route.

eligibility.education: Qualification from an eligible university in the last 5 years
other: Annual cap runs 1 November to 31 October.
Time on this visa doesn't count toward settlement.
Fee, savings and English level not on the page read.

routes.processing: Usually about 3 weeks from outside the UK, about 8 weeks from inside.

routes.name: Scale-up Worker visa
routes.summary: For people with a job offer of at least 6 months from an approved UK scale-up business. First visa is 2 years, then extensions of 3 years.

other: Certificate of sponsorship from an approved scale-up.
Eligible occupation and minimum salary (figure not confirmed).
You usually need to prove English.

routes.processing: Usually about 3 weeks from outside the UK, about 8 weeks from inside.

routes.name: Innovator Founder visa
routes.summary: For experienced businesspeople starting a new, innovative, scalable business in the UK. An approved endorsing body must back the idea. Initial stay 3 years.

other: New, innovative, viable and scalable business idea.
Endorsement from an approved endorsing body (1,000 GBP).
You can't join a business that is already trading.
You must meet your endorsing body at 12 and 24 months.
English required.
Settlement reforms may change timing. Funds requirement not on the page read.

routes.processing: Usually about 3 weeks from outside the UK, about 8 weeks from inside.

routes.name: Student visa
routes.summary: For people 16 or over with a place on a course at a licensed student sponsor. Up to 5 years for degree level. Limited work is allowed.

other: Place on a course from a licensed sponsor.
Enough money for living costs and course fees (figures not on the page read).
English required.
Under 18 needs parental consent.
Dependants allowed only in limited cases, not confirmed. Healthcare surcharge amount not on the page.

stay.note: Up to 5 years for degree courses, up to 2 years below degree level.

routes.processing: Usually about 3 weeks from outside the UK, about 8 weeks from inside.

routes.name: Graduate visa
routes.summary: Lets Student visa graduates stay and work or look for work. 2 years if you apply by 31 Dec 2026, 18 months if you apply from 1 Jan 2027, 3 years after a PhD. Can't be extended.

other: You must be in the UK on a Student visa and have completed an eligible course.
You can switch to Skilled Worker and similar routes later.

stay.note: 18 months for applications from 1 January 2027. 36 months for doctoral graduates.

routes.name: Youth Mobility Scheme visa
routes.summary: Live and work in the UK for up to 2 years if you are 18 to 30 (18 to 35 for some countries) from a participating country.

other: Age limit is 35 for Australia, Canada, New Zealand and South Korea.
Hong Kong and Taiwan applicants must first be selected in a ballot.
Also open to some British overseas nationality holders (British overseas citizens, BOTCs, BN(O)).
India uses a separate scheme.

stay.note: Australia, Canada and New Zealand citizens can extend a year.

routes.name: Family visa: partner or spouse
routes.summary: For partners of British citizens or settled people. Initial stay up to 2 years 9 months. Usually needs a combined income of 29,000 GBP a year, or savings in some cases.

income.note: Lower 18,600 GBP applies to some people who first applied before 11 April 2024. Savings can replace income, amount not confirmed.

eligibility.language: Good knowledge of English (level not confirmed)
other: Partner must be British or settled in the UK.
Can't usually apply from a visitor visa.
Fiance, fiancee or proposed civil partner visa lasts 6 months and doesn't count toward settlement.
Settlement reforms say family members of British citizens keep their current 5-year pathway. Confirm.

stay.note: Extensions of up to 2 years 6 months.

sources.label: GOV.UK: Join family in the UK

routes.name: Family visas: child, parent, adult relative and private life
routes.summary: Other family routes cover children, parents, adult dependent relatives needing long-term care, and people with long UK private life. Each has its own rules.

other: Family member must usually be British or settled. You generally can't apply if they are on a work or student visa, but may be a dependant instead.
Adult relative must need long-term care from the UK relative.
Private life route is for people who have lived in the UK many years. Details not on the page read.

fees.label: Child or parent, from outside UK
Child or parent, from inside UK

sources.label: GOV.UK: Join family in the UK

routes.name: UK Ancestry visa
routes.summary: For Commonwealth citizens with a grandparent born in the UK, Channel Islands or Isle of Man. 5 years, with work and study allowed, then settlement.

other: Commonwealth citizen, British overseas citizen, BOTC, BN(O) or Zimbabwe citizen.
One grandparent born in the UK, Channel Islands or Isle of Man.
Other requirements are on the eligibility page (not read).
Can't switch into this visa from inside the UK.

stay.note: Can extend 5 years or apply for ILR.

routes.name: Common Travel Area (British and Irish citizens)
routes.summary: British and Irish citizens can live, work and study in each other's country, with access to benefits and health services. Covers the UK, Ireland, Jersey, Guernsey and the Isle of Man.

other: Rights rest on the CTA arrangement, not EU membership.
Since 1 January 2026 a valid national identity card can be used to enter the UK, per the page.
The 5 year route to naturalisation for Irish citizens comes from the gov.uk citizenship page. Other CTA specifics not confirmed.

sources.label: GOV.UK: Check how to become a British citizen

routes.name: Indefinite Leave to Remain (settlement)
routes.summary: Permanent right to live, work and study in the UK. Usually 5 years on a work or family route (3 for Global Talent and Innovator Founder). Rules are being reformed, see notes.

other: Work routes: usually 5 years. Global Talent and Innovator Founder: 3 years. Family: via a settled partner, parent or relative. Long residence: 10 years.
Ancestry and BN(O) visas: 5 years.

2025 to 2026 reforms: gov.uk pages describe an earned settlement model with a 10 year baseline, shorter routes (3 or 5 years) for high earners and some public service workers, and longer ones for rule breakers. Family of British citizens and BN(O) holders keep current pathways.
Gov.uk says English must be raised to A-level equivalent, effective March 2027. Existing settled status holders aren't affected.
The pages read gave conflicting dates and no clear start date for the 10 year baseline. Check the current Home Office page before relying on this.

sources.label: GOV.UK news: Home Secretary unveils new rules for migrants settling in the UK
GOV.UK news: Higher standard of English now required to settle
GOV.UK news: Biggest overhaul of legal migration model in 50 years

routes.name: British citizenship by naturalisation
routes.summary: Apply after 5 years of UK residence plus 12 months with ILR or settled status. You need to pass the Life in the UK test, prove English and be of good character.

other: Pass the Life in the UK test.
No more than 450 days outside the UK in the 5 years, and 90 days in the last 12 months.
Good character and intention to keep living in the UK.
Marriage to a British citizen removes the 12-month wait.
Irish citizens: 5 years of UK residence.
Dual citizenship not confirmed. English level and settlement reform effects not confirmed.

citizenship.note: Dual citizenship rules weren't on the pages read.

routes.name: British citizenship for spouses and civil partners
routes.summary: Spouses or civil partners of British citizens can apply after 3 years of UK residence if they hold ILR or EU settled status.

other: Lived in the UK for the last 3 years.
Holds ILR or settled status.
Other conditions (English, Life in the UK test, good character) follow the main naturalisation rules.

routes.name: British citizenship by descent (child registration)
routes.summary: Children born abroad to a parent who is British by descent can be registered in some cases, usually if the parent lived in the UK 3 continuous years before the birth. A British grandparent route exists for the child's parent. Applicants must be under 18.

other: Section 3(2): child born abroad, parent British by descent who had 3 continuous years in the UK (no absence over 270 days). Child becomes British by descent.
Section 3(5): child and both parents lived in the UK 3 years. Child becomes British otherwise than by descent.
Children born abroad to a parent British other than by descent are usually automatically British (not covered in the guidance read).
Over 10s need good character. Two referees needed.
Adult descent claims and fee not confirmed.

citizenship.note: British by descent generally can't pass citizenship to children born abroad.
